notes: Correctness fix, not a performance change. CustomTorchBackend built its stop set from tokenizer.eos_token_id, which for gemma-4-*-it is only <eos> (1); the model's generation config says [1, 106, 50]. The instruct model ends an answer with <turn|> (106), so every custom-* request ran to max_tokens. Both torch backends now use base.stop_token_ids (generation config, else model config, else tokenizer). The fix is bb85b10 (on 8a7b6ce); this record vouches for c6f109e, the merge of origin/main (94e9780, PR #38) into the branch, re-issued so the record is bound to the tip rather than to a commit main's scheduler/telemetry changes landed after. The regression test fails to import at both 8a7b6ce and 94e9780 (no helper) and, with the helper reduced to the old tokenizer-only rule, fails with assert {1} == {1, 50, 106}; passes at bb85b10 and c6f109e. The heavy end-to-end test tests/test_custom_backend_scheduler.py::test_generation_stops_at_end_of_turn fails at 8a7b6ce (106 in the output) and passes at bb85b10 and c6f109e. On cold_start/seen (MPS, E2B, greedy) tokens out went 626 -> 220, every after-fix output a prefix of the before output. Measurements affected: kb-20260918-5906bc13. There is no metric delta to be significant about; the assertion is the measurement.
